Q01.text: How well do the last four weeks reflect the cat’s usual behavior?
Q01.help: Describe the last four weeks, or the shorter time you have known the cat. Do not mix behavior before a change with behavior afterwards.

options.usual: I have known the cat for at least four weeks; this period is usual for them
options.changed: Behavior or living conditions have noticeably changed recently
options.health: This is a period of illness, treatment or noticeable mobility difficulties
options.short: I have known the cat for less than four weeks

Q02.text: Who, apart from adult caregivers, lives with the cat or regularly visits the home?
Q02.help: Select the relevant groups. Children’s names, exact ages and personal details are not needed.

options.other_animals: Other animals, such as rabbits, birds or rodents

Q03.text: Whose presence is most clearly associated with a noticeable difference in the cat’s behavior?
Q03.help: Compare only naturally occurring situations. A difference may also mean more play or contact. Choose several groups if it concerns more than one.

options.none: I have not noticed such a difference
options.other_animals: Other animals, such as rabbits, birds or rodents

Q04.text: How often does the cat start playing on their own when awake and with toys available?
Q04.help: For example, chasing a ball or playing with an object. No toys or no opportunity means unobserved, rather than never.

options.rarely: Rarely, in a minority of these situations
options.sometimes: In about half of these situations
options.often: Often, in most of these situations
options.contextual: Clearly different depending on the situation

Q05.text: Your cat is awake and you calmly offer a familiar toy. What usually happens?
Q05.help: Recall ordinary situations without waking or repeatedly prompting the cat.

options.watches: Watches the toy without pursuing it
options.brief_play: Briefly touches or catches the toy
options.joins_play: Joins in: chases, catches or paws at the toy
options.contextual: Varies with the situation

Q06.text: A familiar person walks past the resting cat. What does the cat usually do?
Q06.help: The person is not approaching or touching the cat. Do not count simply making room to pass.

options.moves_away: Gets up and moves farther away
options.still_tense: Remains motionless in a tense posture
options.contextual: Varies with the situation

Q07.text: There is an everyday sound, such as a cupboard closing. What does the cat usually do?
Q07.help: Recall a naturally occurring situation, excluding alarms or renovation. Do not make a sound for this question.

options.looks: Looks toward the sound and stays
options.still_tense: Remains motionless in a tense posture
options.contextual: Varies with the situation

Q08.text: You are sitting quietly outside feeding time. How does your cat usually engage with you?
Q08.help: Describe contact initiated by the cat with you, the person answering the interview.

options.approaches_contact: Approaches and rubs against me or nudges me
options.stays_apart: Stays farther away without initiating contact
options.contextual: Varies with the situation

Q09.text: You are resting, and comfortable spots are available both near you and farther away. Where does the cat usually settle?
Q09.help: Near means within arm’s reach. Describe a free choice, without holding the cat or offering food.

options.close: Beside me, within reach or on my lap
options.same_room: In the same room, beyond arm’s reach
options.farther: In a comfortable spot farther away
options.contextual: Varies with the situation

Q10.text: Your cat and {other_cat} meet at home. How does your cat usually initiate contact?
Q10.help: Both relationship questions concern the same pair. Being in the same room alone is not a friendly greeting.

options.initiates_greeting: Approaches to rub against or groom the other cat
options.stays_near_without_greeting: Stays nearby without initiating a greeting
options.contextual: Varies with the situation

Q11.text: {other_cat} appears nearby. What does your cat usually do?
Q11.help: Exclude mutual play chases and simply passing one another. Describe moving away from this particular cat.

options.stays: Stays or continues what it was doing
options.moves_away: Moves farther away or to another room
options.changes_route: Changes route or moves higher to avoid getting closer
options.still_tense: Stays, but in a tense posture
options.contextual: Varies with the situation

Q12.text: A new, stationary object appears in a familiar room. What does the cat usually do?
Q12.help: The object is accessible. Recall an ordinary event; do not stage a test.

options.investigates: Approaches and sniffs or examines it closely
options.observes: Observes it from its current spot
options.contextual: Varies with the situation

Q13.text: A previously closed space becomes accessible in the familiar home. What does the cat usually do?
Q13.help: The space is safe and freely accessible. Describe something that has already happened.

options.stays_in_known_place: Stays in the familiar part of the home
options.contextual: Varies with the situation

Q14.text: You serve a familiar meal in the usual spot. What does the cat do before the first bite?
Q14.help: This describes inspecting food, not appetite, eating speed or acceptance of a new food.

options.starts_eating: Starts eating without a noticeable inspection pause
options.inspects_first: First pauses to look or sniff for longer
options.contextual: Varies with the situation

Q15.text: At what height does the cat usually rest when freely choosing a place?
Q15.help: Describe choice, not jumping ability. Elevated includes a seat, furniture back, windowsill or shelf. The scale records frequency of choosing above-floor places, not height in centimeters.

options.mostly_elevated: Mostly on furniture, windowsills or shelves
options.contextual: Clearly different depending on the situation

Q16.text: How sheltered are the places the cat usually chooses to rest?
Q16.help: Sheltered includes a den, under furniture or behind a plant; open includes an exposed rug or open shelf. A furniture back can be both elevated and open.

options.contextual: Clearly different depending on the situation

Q17.text: What alternative resting places are genuinely accessible to the cat?
Q17.help: One answer describes the available choices. Consider closed doors, difficulty reaching a place, and people or animals occupying or blocking it.

options.both: Choice of both height and shelter: low and elevated, sheltered and open
options.height_only: Choice of height, but only one type of shelter
options.cover_only: Choice of shelter, but only one height level
options.neither: Only one type of place is accessible

Q18.text: The cat has settled in its usual resting spot. What do you typically see?
Q18.help: Consider body relaxation and resting. Being motionless alone does not mean being relaxed.

options.settles: Relaxes and rests or falls asleep
options.stays_alert: Remains alert and watches the surroundings
options.cannot_settle: Changes position or leaves without settling
options.contextual: Varies with the situation

F_TARGET.text: Which other cat will you describe in this short interview?
F_TARGET.help: Choose one cat or enter a temporary name. We do not choose automatically. The remaining relationships will stay undescribed.

F_CONTEXT.text: What mainly changes in the cat’s behavior around {group}?
F_CONTEXT.help: Choose the clearest pattern, or several changes. An association with someone’s presence does not establish a cause.

options.withdraw: Moves away or hides more often
options.space: Changes resting places or movement routes

F_SPACE.text: Which description best matches the use of resting places?
F_SPACE.help: This clarifies the conditions. It adds no caution points and does not replace observations of freely chosen calm rest.

options.access: Access to other places is limited or blocked
options.retreat: Mainly goes there after moving away from someone
options.mobility: I notice difficulty climbing or jumping
options.varied: Both calm rest and retreat occur

F_VARIATION.text: The answers about {axis} differ. What might explain this?
F_VARIATION.help: Both answers can be accurate. Do not force them to agree.

options.different_contexts: The situations differ, and the behavior differs with them
options.varies_same_context: The behavior varies even in similar conditions

Barf.title: BARF calculator
Barf.intro: Build a recipe, see its balance, keep every version.
Barf.weightHint: Enter the weight used for this recipe. It is saved with this recipe version.
Barf.suggestionHint: Review the quantity, then add it to the recipe. This replaces any existing quantity of this ingredient.
Barf.suggestionMissing: A quantity cannot be proposed because required nutrient data is missing. Review the missing values in the balance.
Barf.suggestionUnavailable: No quantity can be calculated from these inputs. Start with meat and check the ingredient data.
Barf.sourceNotSpecified: Source not specified in the calculator
Barf.sourceUnverified: Values imported from calculator 1.9c; not independently verified. Check the current label of any supplement.
Barf.emptyIngredients: Search for the first ingredient to begin.
Barf.draftNotice: Working calculation. Nutritional suitability has not been verified.
Barf.invalidDraft: Enter valid weights and quantities to update the balance.
Barf.needMeat: Add meat to calculate portions and reference values.
Barf.massIncomplete: * Known mass only. Capsule or drop mass is missing, so portion weight and moisture cannot be fully calculated.
Barf.missingExplanation: Totals marked * contain missing source contributions. These stay unknown unless an explicit calculation assumption is shown.
Barf.referenceExplanation: Reference values are carried over from calculator 1.9c. They are not universal upper limits or a confirmation of dietary adequacy.
Barf.sourceModel: The original model uses 25 g of meat per kg of cat weight per day. Added animal fats count towards meat weight, as in the source. Nutrient references scale with meat weight. This is not an individual energy assessment or a disease-specific diet.
Barf.roundingNote: Suggestions keep 0.001-unit precision. Intermediate totals are not rounded. Source gaps are retained; any calculation assumption is stated explicitly.
Barf.signInRequired: Sign in to create and save your recipes.
Barf.requestFailed: The request failed. Your unsaved changes are still here. Try again.
Barf.conflict: A newer version was saved elsewhere. Your changes are still here. Reload the saved recipe before editing it again.
Barf.versionMismatch: This recipe uses a different calculation version. Open its saved results or make a new copy with the current data.
Barf.copyReady: A new copy is ready. Review it using the current data, then save.
Barf.saved: Recipe saved. Previous versions are preserved.
Barf.archived: Recipe archived. Its history is still available.
Barf.accessDenied: Access to this account is unavailable. Sign in again or contact the pilot organizer.
Barf.historicalNotice: You are viewing a saved, read-only version. Make a copy to create a new recipe.
Barf.rule_yeast: 3 g yeast per kg of meat
Barf.rule_premix: source premix quantity per kg of meat
Barf.taurineAssumption: Calculation assumption: missing taurine is counted as 0 for: {names}. This does not mean the product contains no taurine.
Barf.planStockHint: Enter the products you have and the maximum available amounts. The planner below will choose quantities and suggest up to 3 products to buy.
Barf.planInstructions: Marked products are used in full. Other meat amounts and supported additives can be reduced to fit the batch. Up to 3 new products may be suggested; available products do not count towards this limit.
Barf.planBatchHint: Defaults to all available meat. To make a smaller batch, unmark the meats that may be left over. Added fat remains part of the original model’s nutrient reference calculation.
Barf.planManualUnit: This item keeps the entered amount. Automatic dosing is limited to source rules with gram units.
Barf.planError: The proposal could not be calculated. Check your quantities and try again.
Barf.planNoProposal: No proposal fits these stock limits and fixed amounts. Check the batch size and the products marked “Use all”.
Barf.planNoImprovement: The search did not find an improvement over your base with the available products and constraints.
Barf.planSearchNote: Assessed {count, plural, one {# candidate model} other {# candidate models}} with all targets together.
Barf.planLimited: The search is bounded. This is the best checked proposal, not proof that no better combination exists.
Barf.planProducts: Products in the proposal · {count} to buy
Barf.planChecks: What matches and what still needs checking
Barf.planCriteria: Nutrient totals are compared with the source references; ratios use Ca:P 1.15, K:Na 1.35, moisture 75% and dry-matter fat 25%. References are not safe upper limits. Missing data and disease-specific suitability remain unassessed.
Barf.planIncomplete: Closest proposal found. Review the remaining deviations from the source targets below.
Barf.planSourceTargetsMet: The available source targets match within calculation precision. This is a working recipe based on the stated assumptions, not a verified complete diet.
Barf.planFoodsHint: Enter your meat, fish, liver, yolks and other food ingredients. Their amounts stay fixed; the calculator will propose supplements without the three-product purchase limit.
Barf.planSupplementsInstructions: Keep the quantities of your meats, fish and other base foods. The calculator fits all available additions together, minimizing combined relative deviations across all targets. Larger differences receive a stronger penalty. This mode has no three-product limit.
Barf.planRemoveSupplements: This mode starts with food ingredients only. Remove the entered supplements or switch to the inventory mode; your entries have been kept.
Barf.planBalanceAfter: Your stock is not a recipe yet. Find and apply a proposal to see its full balance, save it or print it. You can also switch to manual balance.
Barf.allMissingAssumption: Calculation assumption: every missing nutrient value counts as 0. Source records remain unchanged; we will complete them later.
Barf.allMissingExplanation: Values marked * use 0 for missing contributions. Expand the row to see which products use this assumption.
Barf.assumedFor: Assumed 0 for {count, plural, one {# product} other {# products}}
Barf.missingSuggestionAssumption: Missing nutrient contributions count as 0 for: {names}.
Barf.planBalanceCriteria: All available source targets are assessed together, including deficits and excesses. Ca:P 1.15, K:Na 1.35, moisture 75% and dry-matter fat 25% are source targets, not verified clinical optima. Missing nutrient values count as 0; a zero denominator cannot define a ratio.
Barf.planUndefinedRatio: Ratio unavailable (zero denominator or unknown mass)
